author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx talk, Jordan Grace examines the invisible armor we often call power—and why it’s not the point. Power is real. But it’s often something we build to protect ourselves under pressure. Through movement, lived experience, and her work in a women-centered dance community, Jordan shows how this armor can quietly pull us away from ourselves.

This talk is about what happens when the goal shifts—from becoming powerful to being who you already are, and learning to love yourself there. Jordan Grace is a choreographer, entrepreneur, and founder of AREA 54, a nationally recognized dance brand that empowers people to rediscover joy, confidence, and community through movement. After working professionally as both a dancer and recording artist, Jordan saw how the pressures of the entertainment industry often strip people of their authentic selves. Determined to create a space that celebrates individuality, she launched AREA 54, where classes are about more than steps — they are about re
title: How teaching dance helped me rediscover joy | Jordan Grace | TEDxNashvilleWomen

author: TEDx Talks
description: Shannon Fernando opened her TEDxBeverlyGrove 2026 talk with an Ethiopian farmer's description of a crop as a member of the family, then admitted she had traveled there to study it like a resource. What followed was not a story about scarcity. It was a case for asking before building anything. Drawing on nearly two years spent earning trust from officials and farmers to cross the crop over a border for the first time in its history, Fernando closes with the line that gives the talk its title: hunger is not a scarcity problem, it is a permission problem. Shannon Fernando, MSN-FNP-C, is a family nurse practitioner and global nonprofit leader advancing healthcare access, women’s entrepreneurship, and food security for indigenous women and their families in East Africa and South Asia. She is the Founder and CEO of Alabaster International and works directly in remote regions of Kenya, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Sri Lanka to elevate local voices and advance equity and justice for marginalize
title: The Permission Principle | Shannon Fernando, MSN-FNP-C | TEDxBeverly Grove

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world full of chaos and division, honey bees show us how communication and shared purpose can lead to great things. A beekeeper’s talk on what we can learn from the complicated life inside the hive. These practical lessons will help us make better decisions and take action to light up our corners of the world. Rebecca Krowelski is the Marketing & Communications Director at the Alzheimer Society of Manitoba, part of a communications career spanning more than two decades. Outside that work, she is the owner of Prairie Sweetheart Honey and operates a small-scale urban apiary in Winnipeg. 

Krowelski has taken her interest in beekeeping well beyond the backyard. She completed Cornell University's Master Beekeeping Program, has been involved with the Red River Apiarists' Association and Direct Farm Manitoba, and has explored beekeeping as a tool for sustainable livelihoods. Years spent watching colonies survive, adapt and organize themselves gave her a different way of thinking about
title: Why you should think like a bee | Rebecca Krowelski | TEDxWinnipeg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Being different is more than okay! Our unique names are integral to our identities and carry meaningful stories that may not always be ready to be heard but deserve to be told in our own ways, using multiple languages and our authentic voices. A powerful argument for why honouring people’s names is about more than language, it’s about dignity, belonging, and identity. Dr. Xiaoxiao Du is an educator and researcher whose work explores the close connections among language, literacy, culture and identity. She joined the University of Manitoba's Faculty of Education in 2021 as an Assistant Professor of Language and Literacies. Her research includes early literacy, multimodal meaning-making, identity construction, and the different ways children learn across schools, homes and communities. 

Du earned her PhD from Western University, where her dissertation received the John Dearness Memorial Award. She has served as President and Past President of the Language and Literacy Researchers of Ca
title: Say my name, say it right | Xiaoxiao Du | TEDxWinnipeg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) by students in schools is driven by three things: lack of literacy skills; lack of time to develop them; and fear of failing. How artificial intelligence is transforming learning and what educators, students, and parents need to know to stay ahead. Dr. Peter Denton has spent more than three decades examining the relationship between technology, ethics and the societies that create them. His unusually interdisciplinary career spans history, philosophy, religion, science and technology studies, sustainability and education. He holds five degrees, is an ordained United Church minister, has taught at institutions including the University of Winnipeg, University of Manitoba and Royal Military College of Canada, and is the author or editor of several books on technology, sustainability and society. 

Denton has also been involved with UN Environment since 2012 and contributed to the Global Environment Outlook's North American assessment. Across his tea
title: Technology has always been in your head | Peter Denton | TEDxWinnipeg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Medical error is the #3 killer because human brains cannot handle modern data loads. My ingenious idea is that the “best doctor” isn’t human or robot, but a symbiotic partnership that fixes our cognitive blind spots to save lives and billions in waste. A fascinating look at how medicine must combine technology and human empathy to deliver better care in the future. Dr. Rizwan Manji is a physician, researcher and Associate Professor in the University of Manitoba's Max Rady College of Medicine. He completed his MD, PhD and cardiac-surgery training at the University of Alberta before undertaking critical-care training and an MBA at the University of Manitoba. He practices critical-care medicine and conducts research through the Department of Surgery and St. Boniface Hospital. 

His research spans cardiac-surgery outcomes, bioprosthetic heart valves, cardiovascular disease and the biological and cognitive factors that contribute to medical error and physician burnout. That last area has l
title: Why Good Doctors Make Deadly Mistakes and How to Help Them Stop | Rizwan Manji | TEDxWinnipeg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Imagine if universities harnessed their strengths—programs, research, resources, networks—to invest in Indigenous community-based education. Meeting learners where they are could spark transformative change, turning reconciliation from rhetoric to action. A bold vision for how universities and Indigenous communities can move from symbolic reconciliation to true partnership and shared power. Emily Erickson is a Red River Métis educator and program leader whose work centres on bringing post-secondary education closer to Indigenous communities. Born and raised in Winnipeg on Treaty 1 Territory, she graduated from the University of Manitoba's Bachelor of Education program in 2018 and went on to work in community-based education at both Indigenous nonprofit and post-secondary levels. She now serves as Learning Hubs Supervisor at the University of Manitoba, helping deliver university education and training to Indigenous learners in their home communities. 

Erickson is also pursuing a Maste
title: Reconciliation Isn't a Framework—It's a Responsibility | Emily Erickson | TEDxWinnipeg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A DJ’s deeply personal story about sight loss and redefined purpose through creativity and self-expression. Tyler Sneesby, better known to generations of Winnipeg music fans as DJ Hunnicutt, has been making and performing music for more than three decades. He co-founded the independent hip-hop label Peanuts & Corn Records in 1994 and has performed everywhere from Winnipeg clubs to stages in New York, Berlin, Oslo and Bogotá. He has also spent years performing with the acclaimed improv duo Crumbs, taking that work to theatre festivals across Canada and Europe.

Sneesby's creative life changed dramatically after he experienced significant vision loss in 2019. Rather than stepping away from performance, he began finding new ways to DJ and navigate live venues, while becoming an advocate for greater accessibility for blind and low-vision people in music and theatre. He now works as Services Coordinator with VIEW and has also expanded into stage acting with Sick + Twisted Theatre. This tal
title: Hip-hop, hacks and discoveries through disability | Tyler Sneesby | TEDxWinnipeg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A compelling look at how slowing down, reflecting, and truly seeing ourselves can unlock clarity, healing, and stronger leadership. Suzi Friesen has spent much of her career at the intersection of education and mental wellness. She is Director of Educational Programs with the True North Youth Foundation, where she has played a central role in developing Project 11, the foundation's mental-wellness program for students and educators. A former classroom teacher and curriculum developer, she has helped expand Project 11 from Manitoba classrooms to schools elsewhere in Canada and internationally.

Friesen also holds a Master of Arts in Counselling Psychology and is a Canadian Certified Counsellor. Her work draws together education, counselling, resilience and the practical skills people use to understand themselves. Reflection has become a recurring theme in that work: creating enough space to notice the questions, assumptions and experiences that can otherwise remain buried beneath the p
title: The Questions We Carry in Silence - and How to Answer Them | Suzi Friesen | TEDxWinnipeg

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The people we meet, the places we visit, and the experiences we have can shape the course of our lives in ways we never expect.

In this talk, William Precht reflects on the mentors, moments, and discoveries that inspired his journey from a student at SUNY Oswego to a lifelong career studying coral reefs. Through personal stories of curiosity, exploration, and purpose, he explores how inspiration can spark discovery, influence future generations, and motivate action in the face of environmental challenges. William Precht is an internationally recognized expert in coral reef ecology and geology. His career path was solidified while an undergraduate student at SUNY Oswego. In his senior year, Bill had the opportunity to spend a semester studying at the Discovery Bay Marine Lab (DBML) in Jamaica. Combining his love of both geology and ecology (and scuba diving), Bill performed an independent senior research project on the modern reef communities located directly in front of DBML. This li
title: Harnessing Inspiration to Protect Coral Reefs | Mr. William F. Precht | TEDxSUNY Oswego

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Srinath Ravichandran explores how the problems and challenges we face can shape the person we become.

He shares his journey with AgniKul Cosmos and the career transitions that shaped his path, exploring how he approached complex problems, embraced challenges, and grew through solving them.

Through these experiences, he reflects on embracing uncertainty, learning from challenges, and continuously evolving Srinath Ravichandran is the Co-Founder and CEO of Agnikul Cosmos, a pioneering Indian space startup redefining satellite launches through customizable and reusable rockets with breakthrough propulsion technology. Srinath trained as an electrical engineer, and later became a financial derivatives trader, while also attending film school before turning towards his childhood passion in aerospace. After 10 years at Wall Street, Srinath decided to pursue his core interest in space exploration with the idea that getting to space shouldn’t be the hardest aspect of working from or living in
title: Embrace the problem | Srinath Ravichandran | TEDxThiagarajar College of Engineering

author: TEDx Talks
description: Dr. K.P. Karthikeyan explores how ordinary people can create extraordinary change by stepping forward when it matters most. Through stories of courage and compassion, he highlights people who stepped forward to help others at crucial times.  He also shares personal experiences from his journey in public administration, offering insights into the people, challenges, and moments that shaped his perspective on creating meaningful change. Ultimately, he reminds us that we are all part of the system, and that each of us has the power to shape it.  Dr. K. P. Karthikeyan, IAS, is a medical doctor turned civil servant (IAS 2014, Tamil Nadu cadre) and MD, ELCOT, driving IT and emerging technologies. He has served as Tirunelveli District Collector, Madurai Corporation Commissioner and Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Commerce, GoI, and held leadership roles in TIDCO, SIPCOT, Guidance Tamil Nadu, TIDEL Park and SDAT. His Tirunelveli water-management initiatives won National Water Award 2024 for
title: When People Step Up, Change Follows | Dr Karthikeyan K P | TEDxThiagarajar College of Engineering

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Padma Shri Dr. Rajagopalan Vasudevan explores the spirit of Yajna, the selfless act of working together and contributing for the betterment of society without expecting anything in return. 

Drawing from the teachings of Sri Krishna and the Srimad Bhagavatam, he connects this philosophy to his work with plastic waste. 

He shares how he transformed discarded plastic into a resource by creating roads out of plastic waste, turning an environmental challenge into an innovative solution. His journey shows how cooperation, innovation and selfless action can create meaningful change. Padma Shri Dr. Rajagopalan Vasudevan, fondly known as the Plastic Man of India, is a distinguished scientist, educator, and pioneer in sustainable engineering. An emeritus professor at Thiagarajar College of Engineering, Madurai, he revolutionized road construction by developing an innovative technology that incorporates waste plastic into bituminous roads. His groundbreaking work has enabled the construction o
title: The Yajna Spirit | Padma Shri Dr Rajagopalan Vasudevan | TEDxThiagarajar College of Engineering

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Venkatarangan Thirumalai begins with Jane Goodall’s observation of a chimpanzee using a stick to extract termites, revealing how tools have always shaped human thinking and behaviour. 

He explores how inventions, from simple physical tools to modern software and AI, increasingly influence the way we work, think, and live. 

With AI, he suggests that the relationship is changing for the first time, as the tools we create begin to shape their creators in return. Venkatarangan Thirumalai is an author, entrepreneur, and startup mentor dedicated to helping founders build resilient, purpose-driven businesses

He founded Vishwak Solutions in 1996, growing it into a global software services firm with offices in India, Seattle, and London, and later co-founded an AI-driven fintech startup in the US.

An Honorary Microsoft Regional Director since 1999 and an IEEE Senior Member with over 30 years in software, he helps enterprises adopt Generative AI and advises founding teams of funded technolo
title: The Tools We Build,Build Us Back | Venkatarangan Thirumalai | TEDxThiagarajar College of Engineering

author: TEDx Talks
description: A language is more than words—it is a doorway into a culture, its history, humor, traditions, and people. In this engaging and interactive session, Shafeeq Gigyaani takes the audience on a rapid introduction to Pashto, exploring simple words, phrases, expressions, and cultural meanings. The talk turns language learning into an experience while showing how preserving and sharing local languages can help carry cultural identity into the future. Shafeeq Gigyani is Pakhtunkhwa based Activist who pokes in Politics & Governance, Society & Culture and Tech & Entrepreneurship through his Activism, Blog, Podcast & a Radio Show. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Learn Pashto in 18 Minutes | Shafeeq Gigyani | TEDxFAST Peshawar
